articles.title: Tannery Street Digs Out
articles.deck: A month after the river went over its banks, neighbors on Tannery Street are still hauling out silt, and the cleanup has become a block project.
body: Four weeks after the Millrace went over its banks, the mud on Tannerv Street is mostly gone. What’s left is the garages. Along the south end of the street, where the river reached the rafters, the doors are off, the walls are stripped to the studs, and the tools that families couldn’t carry out are sitting in sodden piles at the curb.

Ed Ostrowski’s detached garage at 318 Tannery St. was hit hardest. Ostrowski has kept a workshop in the back since 1968, and he lost a drill press, two workbenches and most of the hand tools he inherited from his father. “The drill press I can replace,” he said Saturday, standing in the doorway with a pry bar. “The drawings my father kept in the bottom drawer are gone.”

Volunteers from St. Brendan’s and Scout Troop 14 came out on three Saturdays to haul debris to the county bins at the end of Mill Road. The Tannery Street block association put a sign-up sheet on every mailbox, and by the third week most houses had a shift assigned.

The county has approved emergency loans for homeowners with flood damage, with an application deadline of July 15. The Red Cross relief fund at St. Brendan’s stands at $14,200. The committee will meet on June 16 at the Eastgate hall to decide how to divide it.
Anyone who wants to help can bring work gloves and a wheelbarrow to the corner of Tannery and Mill on Saturday at 8 a.m. Coffee will be on the Ostrowskis’ back step.

photos.caption: Silt still covers the driveway at 311 Tannerv St. on the morning of May 21.
The Ostrowski garage at 318 Tannery St. the day after the water went down. The line on the back wall marks the high water.
Scouts and St. Brendan’s volunteers load debris from the south end of Tannery Street.
Residents gather under a borrowed tent at the corner of Tannery and Mill for the first block meeting.
